title: Grateful Dead Live at The Strand Lyceum on 1972-05-23
source: MSR>C>DAT>CD>EAC>WAV>SHN via Andy Lemieux encoded by Sean Cribbs

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a high‑energy Europe ’72 show with smoking Dark Star→Morning Dew, stellar Comes A Time and classic transitions.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the luminous soundboard mix that lets the band’s emotional range shine, despite minor hiss and a brief distortion in Morning Dew. Musically the performance is a tour‑high point – Dark Star stretches over half an hour, the NFA→Hey Bo Diddley→NFA segue dazzles, and Comes A Time glows, all delivered with the band on a creative peak.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews are 4‑5 stars and praise both the musical fire‑power and the clean soundboard source; only a few note minor recording flaws, so the weighted rating leans strongly positive.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp, clean and well balanced. Listeners note a faint hiss and a brief scratchy distortion on Morning Dew, but overall the mix is very listenable.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away / Bo Diddley (NFA→Hey Bo Diddley→NFA)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A varied set that weaves classic tunes with extended jams; many tracks later appeared on Steppin' Out, giving a sense of continuity across the Europe ’72 tour.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as delivering 'out‑of‑this‑world fanning' and tones never heard before; his guitar work on Dark Star is highlighted as spectacular.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for laying down a menacing yet warm bass foundation during the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for hitting weird chords that add texture; solid rhythm‑guitar/vocal support throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: The Drums segment in Dark Star→Morning Dew is called wild, out‑of‑control, then calming – a highlight of the performance.
